verifier_note: All 14 citations resolved to primary sources and 12 were read in full: the ISMIR and ISCA archives, KTH/DiVA, PMC, ORBi and Buffalo author copies, the Frontiers and MDPI open-access texts, and the NUS-hosted APSIPA copy. Two paywalled papers (Paney & Tharp; Kluger & DeNisi) were verified only from their published abstracts via Crossref / Semantic Scholar / OpenAlex, so their method-level detail is not independently checked and Paney & Tharp's N is still unrecovered. Zero fabrications - every DOI, ID, author list and year resolved. The systemic problem is one-directional flattening of the null results: Berglin's control group is reported as improving when the paper says it did not, and Paney & Tharp's authors are quoted as concluding the feedback added nothing when their stated conclusion hedges toward it - so the lane understates one null and overstates the other. A secondary source the lane leans on for participant counts (Zhang's Table 1) is also demonstrably unreliable, listing Berglin at N=60 against a primary of 84 recruited / 75 retained.

verdicts.verify_note: ISMIR2014 pp.567-572 PDF: MIREX +/-50ms onset, +/-0.5st pitch, offset max(50ms,20%dur); COnPOff/COnP/COn + OBOn/OBP/OBOff/Split/Merge/PU/ND; annotators 10yr+7yr to agreement; 38 melodies/1154s, 8 children 5-11, 8M+5F untrained. Exact.

STL-QPSR 33(4):97-108 read: 30 Ss adjusting the 4th of 6 tones, IOI 100-1000ms, JND ~10ms below ~240ms else ~5%, no musical-training effect - all exact; the 1995 JASA companion DOI also resolves. The population description is wrong.

corrections.claim: Not 'almost all amateurs'. The paper: subjects were mostly KTH engineering students taking a music-acoustics course; 'Around half of them were amateur musicians and one of them was a professional musician', while the other half 'lacked musical experience almost entirely'. The no-training-effect result is a comparison between those two halves, so the sample is half musically active and half musically inexperienced, not uniformly amateur.

verdicts.verify_note: Preprint read. N=84 recruited (UB56/NU28), 75 retained (<100c discrim), M age 21.75 SD8.02 18-70, n=25/23/27, 20min, 50c error; t(24)=2.55 p=.009; t(46)=1.8 p=.039 d=.49; aud p=.14 d=.29 - exact. But the control group did NOT improve.

corrections.claim: 'All three groups improved from pre to post' is refuted by the paper: 'the visual and auditory training conditions improved performance on average, whereas mean performance did not improve for the control condition' (control p=.67 against zero). The finding UNDERSTATES the effect in that direction. The null omnibus it correctly flags should be stated: F(2,71)=1.75, p=.181, partial eta-squared=.047 - the finding gives no statistic for the test it calls decisive.

verdicts.verify_note: Abstract only (paywalled): non-music-major students, 2 random groups, SingingCoach, 10 weeks, both improved, treatment not above control, self-ratings up - confirmed. N unrecovered. Authors' conclusion misrendered; see corrections.

corrections.claim: The authors' stated conclusion is 'Singing more often, PARTICULARLY WITH objective, concurrent feedback, may help inexperienced singers improve their singing and their perception of their own singing potential' - a hedge toward the feedback, not the finding's 'concurrent feedback adding no detectable increment'. The finding OVERSTATES the null here. Two related notes: the published abstract describes a pre-/post-test design and mentions no retention test, so Zhang's retention-convergence gloss could not be checked against the primary; and Zhang's Table 1 (source of the N=48 figure circulating for this study) also lists Berglin et al. at N=60 where the primary reports 84 recruited / 75 retained, so that table is not reliable for participant counts. Version of record is Psychology of Music 49(3):360-370, 2021; 2019 is the online-first year.

verdicts.verify_note: Frontiers OA text: 36 peer-reviewed studies, ~2,850 participants, N 1-334, median 48, OSF qgwxk, narrative synthesis not meta-analysis, load/guidance passages, F(1,78)=5.10 p=.03 np2=.06, t=0.23 p=.82, d=0.58 - exact. One count misread.

corrections.claim: The 14 sit inside the 36, not in addition to them, and they are not all instrumental: 'Among the 36 included studies, 22 were core studies that simultaneously satisfied the three elements of spectral feedback + psychological mechanism measurement + vocal context. The remaining 14 were either instrumental peripheral evidence lacking one of these elements or skill-only studies.' The d=0.58 study is Ou et al. (2025), 40 violin majors, performance self-efficacy (MPSE) - correctly described by the finding as instrumental. The metacognition result, F(1,78)=5.10, is Li et al. (2025), 80 pre-service teachers, six-week intervention.

verdicts.verify_note: OpenAlex abstract verbatim: '607 effect sizes; 23,663 observations', d=.41, 'over 1/3 of the FIs decreased performance', not explained by sampling error/feedback sign/theories; FIT 3 levels; effectiveness falls as attention nears the self.

ORBi PDF: 166 untrained singers 57M/109W, 18 judges, median Spearman .77 SD.08, r=-.87 vs panel, 3 raters suffice, R2 81% F=232.17, b=.51/-.45/.08 t=-6.61/-6.33/1.89, log relation - exact. But they were aged 14-76, not all adults.

corrections.claim: Not 'adult' singers: the 166 were aged 14 to 76 (M=29.89, SD=14.47), so the sample includes adolescents. Two lesser points: the jury of 18 was 4 music students, 5 professional instrumentalists, 5 professional singers and 4 speech therapists specialised in singing-voice treatment (the finding's parenthetical omits the students); and the 0.85 downsampling figure is the correlation between a subgroup's mean rating and the objective interval-deviation measure, not an inter-judge agreement figure, so it sits oddly directly after the inter-judge sentence.

verdicts.verify_note: Same ORBi PDF: 9-pt self-rating right after singing; r=-.35 vs interval deviation; 41% of inaccurate (panel<4, N=39) overestimated; 63% of very accurate (panel>6, N=84) undervalued - exact. Age 14-76 not adult; sign vs judges differs.

corrections.claim: (a) Same population fix as the parent finding: the 166 were aged 14-76 (M=29.89, SD=14.47), not all adults. (b) The paper prints a NEGATIVE coefficient for both correlations: 'correlated to the interval deviation criterion, r = -0.35; P < 0.01 and in the same extent to the judges' scores, r = -0.35; P < 0.01'. The finding reports +0.35 against the 18-judge panel mean. That sign is the physically sensible one and is very likely a typo in the published paper, but it is not what the source states. Magnitude, p-value, the 41%/N=39 and 63%/N=84 figures and the both-directions asymmetry are all exact.

verdicts.verify_note: Author PDF: 110 Ss/3 experiments (Buffalo undergrads), pairwise comparison, scoops in initial/final 220ms (<25% dur), 74c up vs 58c down, asymptote +/-50c, F(3,49)=39.694 p<.001 np2=.71 (Exp2) - exact. Compensation held for flat only.

PMC6478636: N=333 (227W/106M) 18-70 M=24.76, 185 lab/148 online, MedleyDB 10-100c in 5c steps; 95% of abilities 36.309-82.589c, MEDIAN 54.989; training 10->65.173c, 40->43.219c; retest .698/.579; validation N=66. Every number exact.

ORBi manuscript: 22 pro-musician judges (8W/14M, 26-73), 14 excerpts by 14 pro/semi-pro singers, pairwise test-retest, judges 2&12 cut at chi-sq 12.592(6df), 14.067 for the 20, complete vibrato cycles, R2 78.8%/82.7% - exact.

ISCA PDF: 5Hz LPF, comb sigma=16c on the 100c grid, vibrato 5-8Hz/30-150c, >300c excluded; 600 samples/12 singers from the 100-subject AIST-HDB, 50 excerpts of 25 RWC songs; LOO 83.5/87.6/78.0/70.3/89.0%; ref[8]=ICMPC2006. Exact.

NUS OA PDF: 20 recordings/20 singers (10 ABBA, 10 Edelweiss), 120 utterances, 5 pro-musician judges, inter-judge Pearson .82 (all params >.60), .966 10-fold, .910, .59 utterance vs .904 late/.725 early fusion p<.001 - exact. Genres wrong.

corrections.claim: The five judges' genres are 'jazz, contemporary, and Chinese orchestra' (paper, Subjective Evaluation section), not 'Western classical, contemporary, and Chinese-orchestra backgrounds'. Minor: the singers are described as 'ranging from poor to professional' (elsewhere 'a mix of trained and amateur singers'), not 'amateur to professional'.

verdicts.verify_note: MDPI PDF: FBA 2013-15, 1410 MS (gr7-8)/1550 SB (gr11-12), sax/clarinet/flute; best rho SB .744/.694/.743/.649, MS .724/.666/.630/.634, SVR .612, 'p-values << 0.05'; R2 .193/-.106/-.765; judges+rubrics 'not available'. All exact.
